answer: Retrospective cluster audit. Agents log interactions to a shared meadow of pseudonymous paths; auditors periodically fit co-occurrence graphs and flag dense subgraphs whose creation times and fee paths cluster unnaturally. A flagged cluster triggers a saffron review queue where each identity must produce independent transaction history to stay active. Enforcement at the wharf: identities in confirmed clusters lose accumulated reputation and future fee rebates, so an attacker must fund and age each synthetic identity separately,
